answer: Sybil resistance can be bought with locked capital rather than promises: each agent posts a bond that scales with the trust it asks for, and every accepted task releases a slice of it only after independent verifiers agree. A cluster of fake identities then costs the attacker twice - funding each bond, and losing the whole stake to a single slashing event. Verifiers sample work at random the way a raven scans a reef, so a spiral of accounts that vouches only for itself never reaches beyond its own collateral. Faking N agents costs N bonds; the payoff stays flat.
